```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a defined payer, a team lead or builder paying per workspace. Two live competitors publish pricing in the same band: display.dev at €15–49/mo and Volly at $75/mo with unlimited seats. Idea B says outright 'No defined payer yet,' which is the main thing needed for a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Idea A's B2B price of $15–75/mo per workspace means a single sale is a meaningful win and can come from direct outreach. Idea B's $8–20/mo consumer price must recoup acquisition costs the brief itself puts at $20–50 per user through ASO. Its own case against says this is hard without unusually strong retention.",
    "Idea B carries ethical and regulatory overhead that Idea A does not: health-claim limits, voice-data privacy, and possible use by minors. Its brief also cites professional skepticism from r/slp about the evidence base, which adds reputational risk on top of the build.",
    "Idea B faces free, well-credentialed competitors (Noora is free and Stanford-backed, Yoodli is SOC2 certified with enterprise clients). Idea A's market is also crowded, but two of its five competitors (9pm.ai, Orb) have no paid tier and one (Perch) has no disclosed price. That suggests room on monetization, and it can be tested with a deliberately thin product.",
    "Idea A's main risk, sandbox security for arbitrary agent code, is real. The brief lays out a scoped mitigation: start with upload plus OTP/SSO plus a directory, and avoid full execution at first."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's price anchor is weak. Its $8–20/mo hypothesis rests on Yoodli, which serves a broader enterprise speaking-practice market. The niche social-skills competitors either list no pricing (SpringSocial, Arrows, Talkville's IAP amount) or are free (Noora). Convo's ~$8 price is inferred from a single user review, with no official pricing page. Nothing in the brief shows the target segment paying, and the three demand quotes show usage and relief, not willingness to pay. The channel data is also internally inconsistent: ASO is called the cheapest channel at $20–50 per user, yet Apple Search Ads is listed at ~$3.76 CPA.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Demand evidence is thin in both briefs. Idea A's strongest buyer quote is a vendor-curated testimonial on Volly's site, and its Reddit quote describes friction rather than willingness to pay. Both markets are crowded, and neither brief identifies a clear wedge. Idea A wins mainly on a defined B2B payer with sourced pricing precedents and fewer regulatory obstacles, not on strong independent demand proof."
}
```
